page.title: Metanoia 2.3: Walkable vs. Streamable
page.description: Discusses various models for navigating data sources

content.p: There are at least three models for navigating data sources. I've named these models "Walkable", "Streamable Push", and "Streamable Pull". While Raku has leaned strongly towards the Streamable models (due to the benefits in concurrency), it uses the Walkable model for grammars -- that's what backtracking is all about.

tr.td: More flexible in coding; makes the easy things easy
Better for large data sources, and for concurrency
Better for large data sources, and for concurrency
Comes with restrictions that make it more difficult to use

content.p: Two new roles will need to be added to Raku to support the generic sources (rather than just the grammar-specific Str). These are:

ul.li: The Walkable. This indicates that the data structure is walkable, and has a method that provides a Cursor. The data structure in question might be a Str, a Tree, or a Table.

Each Walkable has one or more Cursors that indicates the current point in a walkthrough of the data structure. The difference between a Cursor and a Iterator is that a Cursor can be walked backwards, and can skip forwards/backwards through the Walkable. This is less parallelisable than an Iterator, but is necessary for backtracking (which is important both in Regexes and in Logic Programming).

content.p: In this case, it's useful to compare the sources by type.
